title: Coverage of Guessed Output Words
statement: Let $M$ be a finite deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $x,v$ be finite Boolean words and $T$ a natural number; assume $M$ computes output $v$ on input $x$ in exactly $T$ steps. For every choice word $w$ of length $T$, there is a word $u$ of length $|v|$ such that the guessing-phase machine run under $w$ ends at the configuration formed from the $T$-step configuration of $M$ and the captured buffer $u$; conversely, every word $u$ of length $|v|$ occurs in such a configuration for some choice word $w$ of length $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
replaced: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine over the binary alphabet that computes an output $v$ on input $x$ within $T$ steps. Then every choice word of length $T$ drives the guessing-phase machine of $M$ from its initial configuration on $x$ to the invariant configuration for the $T$-step run of $M$, with some captured word of length $|v|$; and conversely, every word $u$ with $|u| = |v|$ is the captured word of that configuration for some choice word of length $T$.
